content: Bacilli are a type of bacteria that are rod-shaped. While most bacteria exist as individual cells, some bacilli have a tendency to adhere to one another. Certain species of these bacteria, such as Mycobacterium tuberculosis, are capable of causing tuberculosis in humans. The term Bacillus, when capitalized and italicized, specifically refers to a genus of bacteria. However, the lowercase term bacillus is often used more generally to describe any single rod-shaped bacterium. In this broader sense, bacilli can be found across various taxonomic groups of bacteria. Similarly, Bacilli (capitalized) refers to a specific bacterial class that includes the genus Bacillus, while bacilli (lowercase) refers to any rod-shaped bacteria, regardless of their taxonomic classification. It is important to note that the term bacillus, when used to describe cell morphology, does not necessarily imply that the bacterium is Gram-positive. For example, Escherichia coli (E. coli) is a rod-shaped bacterium that is Gram-negative. Taxonomically, the class Bacilli belongs to the division (or phylum) Firmicutes. This class includes the orders Bacillales and Lactobacillales. Within these orders, the genus Bacillus is found, along with other Gram-positive bacteria such as Listeria.
